tenures.bio:
Fans.

You know what they are, don’t you? The people who follow this sport like a religion, the people who pump money into the corporate wallets of the massive wrestling companies that pay us, the people who sacrifice their bodies for the fans to get paid. I’ve spent the last 6 years of my life doing this, breaking my arm twice, and breaking my ribs a total of 5 times. Fun, isn’t it?

No, not at all.

I don’t wrestle for anyone other than myself.

Fuck the fans.

I couldn’t care less about the people who live this sport from outside of the ring; they’re not the ones who bleed for a paycheck. The ‘fans’ aren’t the ones, who put their bodies on the line up to 6 nights a week for 30 minutes, are they? Hell no.

The fans are only there for the cheap gimmick matches, that’s the only time those ungrateful bastards are ever happy with what we do. When they don’t get something they like from us, they bitch about it on their online ‘fan forums’...what a crock of shit. They’re only pleased when we split our heads open and bleed profusely. The ‘fans’ are never satisfied with what we do, no matter how much damn pain we put our bodies through, they’re not satisfied.

So this is why I hate the fans.

This is why I hate it when they cheer me. I don’t care for them or their damn opinions of me. When they cheer for me I put on a fake smile, and when they boo I really smile...because when they boo me I can really tell them what I think of their false opinions.

If you don’t like this, then fuck you.

I wrestle for one person, and his name is my name. I don’t wrestle to make you happy, I do it to make me happy? And you know what’s the best part of it?

I get paid to beat people up.

Therefore, I am cool. And you are not.

Fuck the fans. And fuck you.

Match History

Crossroads:

Cassius Deamont [c] Vs. Chris Matthews

First Blood Match

Rush Wrestling World Heavyweight Title Match

On June the 16th, Chris Matthews gave a way a shot at winning the RUSH World Championship for his ‘friend’ (and I stress that a lot) Cassius Deamont. Brooding with jealousy ever since then, Matthews turned on Deamont, erupting in an epic feud that’s included kidnapping, car explosion and lots – and lots of blood. In an unusual twist of events, the loyalties of the fans had slightly switched with now the favouritism flagged onto the shoulders of Cassius Deamont, and the boo’s of hatred now worn on Chris Matthews’s head. The match? Brutal. That one word could summarize what happened, but unfortunately, it doesn’t. Deamont and Matthews put each other through a living hell for the 2nd time in 3 weeks, the only thing keeping each other going was the RUSH Wrestling World Championship. Deamont slammed weapons over Matthews’s skull, his chest, legs, hitting move after move but the challenger kept on fighting back. Deamont made Matthews bleed. But unfortunately the referee had been knocked out mere moments before, Matthews scrambled around trying to clear up his own blood, until...

Intense booing.

Chris Sloboda.

The man who lost the RUSH Wrestling Franchise to former PCW Extreme Champion Rush Mason made his way down to ringside and immediately began to beat down his former I.R.S. Plan cohort Cassius Deamont. Boda didn’t just beat down Deamont – no, no, no. That’s not Boda’s style, we all know that. The Ameri-Czech Bad Ass literally ripped out Deamonts heart and squeezed a river of blood from him, ending the match. The referee saw Cassius bleeding, and not Matthews.

A new champion was crowned.

Result: Win

Adrenaline 13:

Scott Cage, D-Kay Calyx & Brock Newbludd Vs. Chris Matthews

Gauntlet Match

Scott Cage. D-Kay Calyx. Brock Newbludd. Three of RUSH’s finest wrestlers took on the solitary Chris Matthews in a Gauntlet Match that had Matthews’s shot for the title at the Crossroads Pay Per View on the line. Scott Cage was easy pickings for Chris Matthews in this match, defeating the current Network Champion easily. D-Kay opposed a much greater challenge for Matthews in his 2nd fight of the Gauntlet match, both Matthews and Calyx traded a few punches before Calyx hit several high impact. Calyx started to gain the advantage after a more than vile low-blow from Calyx. With a quick fight back attempt, Matthews low-blowed Calyx and quickly slammed down the man who once teamed with Red Rock (HA!) with the Alpha Omega to win the gauntlet match, and a shot back at Deamont at the Crossroads PPV.

Enter Brock Newbludd.

Newbludd dashed into the ring, slamming a chair over Matthews’s skull. With a quick fight back, Matthews leaped back to his feet and nailed Newbludd with the discarded chair, just the cameras went to a commercial break.

Brock Newbludd- 1 | Chris Matthews- 3

Result: Win

Adrenaline 12:

Cassius Deamont & D-Kay Calyx Vs. Chris Matthews

Handicap Match

A handicap situation was forced upon Chris Matthews, the I.R.S. Plan members D-Kay Calyx and rival Cassius Deamont. Being the typical egotistical person that he is, allowed his partner in crime D-Kay Calyx to wrestle for more than ¾ of the match. Matthews and Calyx wrestled very evenly till about half way through this match, until Cassius Deamont demanded to be tagged in – Calyx tagged in the current champion. Deamont only stayed in the ring for a mere minute before tagging back out to the already exhausted D-Kay Calyx. Matthews dived back to his feet, and began to immediately send punch after punch, kick after kick all meant for the skull of Cassius Deamont. Matthews poured on the attacks, until Calyx fought back with a low blow, distraction ended the match for Cassius and D-Kay. Why? Deamont turned his back to Calyx after the blind tag, and was caught by surprise with a roll-up from Matthews. Matthews defeated Deamont & Calyx with a simple roll-up.

Result: Win

Adrenaline 11:

Cassius Deamont [c] Vs. Chris Matthews

Rush Wrestling World Heavyweight Title Match

After weeks and weeks of fighting, feuding against each other, Chris Matthews finally had earned his shot at Cassius Deamont and the much wanted, much prized Rush World Championship. After winning a Fatal Four Way Table Match last week, Matthews finally got his shot. The epic match between Deamont and Matthews raged on for over 30 minutes, with near pinfalls galore. For what seemed impossible Matthews had the advantage for nearly ¾ of this World Title match. 2 Fall Before Me’s from Deamont couldn’t keep Matthews down, nearly could two submission holds. Matthews delivered several high impact moves, the highlight of the match is when Matthews locked on a Dragon Sleeper, but then quickly turned it into the famed Krayzie Death Slam. He went for a pin, but guess who showed their ugly face?

Chris Sloboda.

Boda made his way down to ringside and attacked Matthews, sending him into a pin by Deamont. 1..2..3. It was a cheap win for Cassius Deamont, he wouldn’t of won had it not been for sudden attack by Boda. The whole army ran out. Vulcan Flare, Rich Cannon, Tim Walden and D-Kay Calyx. Like a pack of wolves the entered the ring, Deamont boasting about his win, talking down the bloodied and exhausted Matthews. A match was signed for the PPV, Cassius Deamont Vs. Chris Matthews in a First Blood Match, Cassius signed it with the blood that oozed from Matthews’s head. The I.R.S. Plan retreated to the back, leaving Chris Matthews unconscious on the mats of the ring.

Result: Loss

Adrenaline 10:

Brock Newbludd Vs. Chris Matthews Vs. Tyler Valentine Vs. D-Kay Calyx

A shot at Cassius Deamont’s World Championship was on the line in this Fatal Four-Way Table Elimination match. Chris Matthews was the heavy favourite to win this match, and at advance onto to fight Deamont the week after. What more could you say about a table match like this other then, excitement? You’re right. As an outside chance, D-Kay Calyx didn’t last long in the match, eliminated within a matter of minutes by Tyler Valentine, who in turn, was eliminated a few seconds after. This brought it down to the favourite Chris Matthews, and possibly the most violent man in Rush, Brock Newbludd. Interim owner, the feared and hated Chris Sloboda soon made his way out to ringside, trying to insure a win for his group, a Bounced Czech to Matthews. Newbludd attempted to retreat up to the back, thinking he had it won. A fan, a fat fan distracted Boda at ringside allowing Matthews to escape from the grasp of Boda and to eliminate Brock Newbludd by slamming a Superkick into Newbludd’s chest and driving him through a table with it, thus ensuring a victory for the man from Montreal and a shot at Cassius Deamont, the following week.

Brock Newbludd- 1 | Chris Matthews- 2

Adrenaline 7

The Shack-Pack & Jeremy Howard Vs. The Solution

Tim Walden had booked this 8-Man Tag, originally a 7-Man tag match, to show the unity of the Solution. Unaware that owner Jeremy Howard was lurking in the back, just as the match was about to begin, Howard came out and pencilled himself into the match, his fist since PCW Spring Fling 2002. The now 8-Man Tag was wild and out of control, brawls erupted between the two teams with members of each pairing off with each other. This went on for several minutes, with the chaos stopping at when everyone, bar Cassius Deamont and Christopher Shackelton. After a good 5 minutes in the ring, Deamont went to tag Matthews but the Martial Artist turned around and spat in the champions face. Soon Deamont and Matthews started brawling, they brawled all over the arena, the end result was Chris Matthews having water dumped on him, and then electrocuted. The match was over, El Spiffy! had got the win for team Shack-Pack.

Result: Loss

Ignition Part II

Tex Kelley Vs. Chris Matthews

#1 Contenders Match

The conciliation match for the losers of the prior World Title-status Match. Tex Kelley and Chris Matthews had a shot to become the #1 Contender to the World Title. This was a highly physical and intense match, both men having advantages over the other, but toward the end of the match Matthews had a total domination, ready to finish CTK off, had it not been for Steve Brent’s ignorance. Brent ran down to the ring, and Matthews was pushed into a steel chair. Tex Kelley won, an irate Chris Matthews was left to fight another day...

Result: Loss

Ignition Part I

Cassius Deamont & Jonathan Drachen Vs. Chris Matthews & Tex Kelley

This match was to determine which two would face off for the RUSH World Title in the main event. The match was wild, that would be an understatement to say the least. All 4 men gave it their all, punch after punch they received and delivered. Drachen and Deamont were the bitterest of enemies, Kelly and Matthews weren’t on good terms with each other either. In typical Chris Matthews fashion, he and his team started to take advantage toward the end of the match, him and CTK about to win their spot in the Main Event. Drachen and Kelley paired off as did Deamont and Matthews, Matthews was taking Deamont apart. Walden and Brent made their way out to the ring, CTK and Drachen suddenly went to fight them, but it was all over for CTK as back in the ring, Chris Matthews laid down for Cassius Deamont sending him into the main event.

Result: Loss

Adrenaline 6

Tex Kelley & Jonathan Drachen Vs. Cassius Deamont & Chris Matthews

A week before all 4 men would meet to decide who would go onto be crowned the first RUSH Champion. Earlier in the night, during a taped segment of a martial arts lesson between Chris Matthews and Cassius Deamont’s two, yes TWO, bi-sexual valets, Matthews had made advances on them. They had ran off and told Cassius, but he didn’t believe them. During the match, Cassius and Matthews pretty much dominated Drachen and CTK, they eventually picked up the pin via a steel pipe shot from Steve Brent. Suddenly Jeremy Howard made his way out to the stage, and aired the footage of the Martial Arts lesson. Deamont looked at Matthews and attacked him. Punch after punch until Tex Kelley and Jonathan Drachen cleared out all members of The Solution with steel chairs.

Result: Win

Adrenaline 5

Tex Kelley & Jonathan Drachen Vs. Chris Matthews & Steve Brent

Jonathan Drachen and Tex Kelley took on Chris Matthews and his Solution Stable Mate, Steve Brent. This was a back and forth match for roughly 10 minutes, a few tags made, nothing really spectacular. Tex Kelley pinned Chris Matthews, mainly due to Steve Brent’s laziness to contribute.

Result: Loss

Adrenaline 4

Skye Stone Vs. Chris Matthews

One of the most physical matches in RUSH’s short history as Chris Matthews and Skye Stone went to battle again. Back and forth this match went with Stone and Matthews showing their talents in front of the large crowd on hand. Suddenly the majority of the main event scene had burst out of their locker rooms, each trying to get a piece of each other. Each one paired off against each other in their respective feuds. Hiro Saotome proved to be Skye Stone’s downfall, he and Matthews traded a Martial Arts kicks, until Matthews bustard a concrete clipboard over Saotomes head, pinning him and taking the win.

Result: Win

Adrenaline 3

Jonathan Drachen, Skye Stone & Hiro Saotome Vs. Cassius Deamont, Chris Matthews & Steve Brent

The Good Guys Vs. The Bad Guys. Mayhem described this 6-Man tagged match. Each of the 6 men paired off, 3 separate brawls all over the ring. The action was fast and furious (no, not the movie, that had cars), punch after punch, kick after kick. Team Good Guy was getting the advantage toward the end of the match until “Coach” Tex Kelley came sprinting down the ramp, and eliminated Skye Stone. Deamont got the pin on Saotome. After the match, The Solution decided to have a little fun. Deamont ordered a cage to be lowered, Matthews handcuffed the 3 Good Guys to the cage, Deamont lit the cage on fire. Max Crimson came to the saviour of the good guys, pulling the cage apart with his bare hands...damn Godzilla.

Result: Win

Adrenaline 2

Jonathan Drachen Vs. Chris Matthews

Two Martial Artists fighting it out in the ring. This wasn’t a wrestling match, both men were accomplished Martial Artists, Drachen and Matthews didn’t wrestle in this match. They were trying to out-Martial Art each other, in a way. It went back and forth, both men having equal advantage until Matthews dumped Drachen outside of the ring...and then they swooped down to the ring. Brent and Deamont hit the ring, combined with Matthews they knocked Drachen out with a sickening chair shot! Tex Kelley sprinted down to the ring, only to be cut off by Skye Stone, the three Solution members went back to the beat down of Drachen until Maxx Crimson and Hiro Saotome came charging out from the back. A massive brawl erupted between all the parties involved, everyone brawling all over the place.

Result: Disqualification

Adrenaline 1

Skye Stone Vs. Chris Matthews

His first match in RUSH Wrestling. The Hippie Skye Stone took on Chris Matthews in a highly intense match, a highly technical match. No brawling between the two evenly matched competitors at all throughout the match, wrist locks replaced punches and hammer locks replaced kicks. Stone nearly had the match won, until Matthews turned around and nailed Stone with an impressive Super Enziguri. Then came Matthews’s finisher, but Skye Stone somehow kicked out. Suddenly, Cassius Deamont ran out from the back and distracted the referee, allowing a beat down of Skye Stone. Tex Kelley soon made his way down to the ring, his intentions clear after a few seconds. Then a fight between Kelley and Stone erupted before Kelley got onto the mic and blabbed about crap for a while.

Result: No Contest

tenures.bio:
Physical Description:

Brendon has his share of muscles, but not as much as many of the RUSH stars. He wears his four packed abs proud and his calves are a medium type size. His face description is as follows, blue eyes, short blonde hair, a short horizonal scar under his left eye, a regular sized nose. Weighing in at a mere 187 lbs. and standing tall at 6'0'' Brendon could be called the cruiserweight of RUSH.  Brendon's skin color is a mixture of both tan and white.

Entrance:

The crowd is silent.  Suddenly trumpets sound playing 'Livin' La Vida Loca' by Ricky Martin blasts the stage.  Brendon 'Stimpo' Stimson shoots out from the entrance way wearing a short black hat covering his short blonde hair underneath.  The crowd cheers on Stimpo for his dancing entrance.  He comes out snapping his fingers and dancing to his own style of music.  Wearing a skin-tight black shirt and black trousers with no print on them, he continues to do his latin style dancing to the up-beat song.  The song reaches the chorus as Stimpo's shirt and pants rip off revealing his wrestling outfit consisting of no shirt and his black opaque spandex with 'Stimpo' printed on them in blue letters.  Of course, not forgetting his lucky mask with the many attracting colors.  His face his sheltered by the mask except for his blue eyes.  While still dancing his way down the ring, the Latin PoP star does a neat spin while taking his hat off and frizbeeing it out into the crowd for one lucky fan's dream to come true.  Stimpo finally dives under the bottom ropes ending the song and unfortunantly, his dancing.

Wrestling Attire and Street Attire:

While Wrestling:

Brendon wears no shirt while wrestling but does wear black spandex with 'Stimpo' printed in blue letters, jaggedly designed going down each side. Brendon also wears the same colored boots as his spandex all laced up and ready to go. He never attends the ring without his lucky charm however, that being his mask. A perfectly shaped mask for Brendon's face making room for eye holes and room for his mouth. The mask has many different designs upon it including stripes of color across the mask, around the mask. (it looks similar to Rey Masterio's)

Street clothes:

Brendon covers his face once more by wearing his mask which he believes is his entire wrestling culture. He often wears his tights for wrestling all the time with no shirt on ready to wrestle.

History:

Born on September 28th, 1979 in his hometown of Rochester, New York, Brendon 'Stimpo' Stimson was born. No one knew the future of this boy, how could they? He did have motives to join wrestling however, and it all started in his elementary years...

When he was a wee little boy, Brendon always got his share of mockery from others. Most of these jokes were either short jokes or weak jokes or even jokes about his nickname, 'Stimpo,' each chipping away at Brendon a little at a time. Everyday during the third grade, Brendon would get into fights and always end up on the ground with a new bruise.

Going through his elementary years, Brendon always swore to get his revenge on the bullies who always made fun of him. He finally got to high school, passing by flying colors I might add. High school did have it's other share of problems but this is when Brendon started taking culture classes for the culture of Mexico. He saw that many great wrestlers came from Mexico and thought why not give westling a try.

Sure enough, Brendon started taking wrestling classes and joined the wrestling team at his High school. This began his problems, the teasing once again began. Other kids on the team claimed Brendon was too small and too weak, he may have fit this description being 5'4'' and weighing 105 lbs. at the time. But, Brendon would not have this going on, he decided that he would finally take his anger out onto wrestling opponents proving that he too could be one of the 'cool' kids in his grade.

His first match came, he was put up against a man at least four times his size. 'Not a problem.' Brendon said to himself and went into that match with his head up high with his little muscles flexing. Surprisingly to his fellow classmates, the match lasted for quite a while but Brendon took what he had learned from both his Mexican culture class and his Wrestling lessons by performing what is now called a hurricanrana slamming the huge man down to the mat, head first. Though this move was illigal, Brendon was disqualified but it seemed that his wrestling teammates did not care, they still think today that Brendon is one of the greatest wrestlers in that High School.

So Brendon had broken out of his shell in his wrestling abilities. He thought to himself that if he can't cut it in regular wrestling, why not join one of the modern federations for his style of wrestling. Sure enough, right outside of school door one day was a poster for applications to the DWA-Dark Wrestling Alliance.

Brendon skipped school that day for a good reason, to apply to the Dark Wrestling Alliance at the age of 21, the age he is now. The application was of a long format but Brendon managed to get it done in under 20 minutes, then came his first match for the DWA. He ended up facing one of his long time friends from his High School who called himself, Zarcon.

The match began as normal on March 10th and Brendon gave it all he had. The momentum went back and forth before Brendon finally performed what he used to call the Stimpo Splash, a 540 splash off the top rope. The crowd was stunned at the amazing feet that this new kid could get, he won his debut then went on to win about 8 more matches along with a few losses.

Then, on April the 23rd of 2002, Brendon had a match on the DWA's pay per view called Hostile Takeover. The match was a triple threat between New-Blood (double champion, light heavy weight and hardcore.) and Inferno and of course, Brendon. The first fall of this match was for the light heavy weight title and the other fall was for the hardcore title. The match raged on for what felt to be at least an hour before Brendon finally broke out of his shell once more when both men were down, he climbed up to the top turnbuckle and smashed them both down with that Stimpo Splash. The referee counted the 1...2...3 that day, in which it changed 'Stimpo's' career.

After the win, Stimpo came back to the ring the next night on Monday Night Manic and told the crowd that it was a new Stimpo. He came down the ramp with a small black shoe box. When he told the crowd of fans that he was about to start a new Stimpo, he pulled out from the box a mask! He claimed that this was Stimpo's new style, a Lucadore.

Then it was announced that High Voltage Wrestling was looking to merge with another federation, sure enough, DWA jumped on the opportunity and Stimpo went for the ride. June 15th was the date the merge happened and after the first week of action, (Stimpo winning his first match over Jman.) the new HVW/DWA was sent straight into Primetime Central becoming a network promotion.

Though, HVW was not what Stimpo was looking for in the federation he wanted. So, after about three weeks of action in HVW, (all wins.) Stimpo left HVW in hopes of climbing the WrestlingTattler ladder and maybe have a chance at getting into perhaps one of the top federations. Taking advice from friends, Stimpo entered himself into the Primetime Wrestling Academy to both develop his skills and maybe get into a larger federation.

So his first match in the PWA was a 7-man cemetary match in which he was one of the last men to be eliminated. Taking the loss very well, Stimpo bounced back and won 3 straight matches. Then, Stimpo was ranked in the top ten for those three straight weeks and for the month of June, Stimpo was named the third best wrestler in the PWA.

Then the time came for promotions. Stimpo waited in great anticipation, biting his nails as to what federation was promoting and who was in. The first to promote was NTICW, to Stimpo's depression, he was not on the list but then another federation claimed they were promoting. Stimpo looked at the name and it read in clear letters: CHZ.

Stimpo's self esteem was sky high that day, then he listened and sure enough his name was the second on the list. He jumped up and down and packed his bags immediatly. He flew on the earliast fight to Canada where he became a star of the Canuck Heat Zone.

Brendon only stayed in the CHZ for a mere three weeks until he stands here now, a proud wrestling member of the RUSH federation.  In hopes of making an impact here in RUSH, Brendon may find himself up against WrestlingTattler's best.

Though his name may not be known yet, Brendon 'Stimpo' Stimson has been trying to get known for almost half a year. Yes, for 5 months now, Brendon has attempted to carry his career on sheer determination to get back at the ones who ridiculed him from the past.

Match Archive:

Adrenaline 15

Stimpo was placed in a match with Biohazard for his debut.  The match went on for a while before Biohazard refused to lose to the newcomer and gave him a quick low blow then landed his finisher to Stimpo as he pinned him in his first match in RUSH.

Result: Loss (0-1-0)

Adrenaline 16

His second match, he faced a newcomer in RUSH, John McBride.  McBride debuted and lost his first match just as Stimpo did.  Both men tried their best but it came down when Andi the Magnificant distracted McBride long enough for Stimpo to get a roll-up pin making the ref count to three for his first win.

Result: Win (1-1-0)

Adrenaline 17

A triple threat match between Livewire, John McBride and of course, Stimpo.  Back and forth and back and forth the match went between all three men all countering moves, breaking up three counts until Stimpo found McBride laid out on the mat and landed his teacher's move, the Spiffy! elbow getting the win.

Result: Win (2-1-0)

Adrenaline 18

After winning the triple threat, Stimpo had a shot at the Network title, but didn't show up since later in the show, Spiffy! awarded Stimpo the Syndacite title!

Result: Nothing (2-1-0)

Adrenaline 19

Spiffy! then faces Stimpo in Adrenaline 19 for the belt that was awarded to Stimpo but 'Spiffy!' or was it Spiffy!?  Frustrated with how the match was going, Stimpo took the title and slammed it over Spiffy!'s head disqualifying himself.

Result: DQ Loss (2-2-0)

Adrenaline 20

A neutral battle between Stimpo and CTK where CTK was about to win but Stimpo insisted on using some brass knuckles while the ref wasn't looking laying CTK out flat then soaring into the air landing a huge Stimpo Splash for the cover of 1...2...3.

Result: Win (3-2-0)

Return from the Ashes

Finally, the day came where Spiffy! and Stimpo go head to head in a WCW Hardcore Match.  Back and forth the historic match went until Stimpo went 20 feet in the air off part of the RUSHtron but missed his trademark Stimpo Splash which left Spiffy! to capatalize by landing a huge 50-foot border jump crushing Stimpo under him as the Kodak moment of the match ended with Stimpo and Spiffy! both leaving in ambulances.

Result: Loss (3-3-0)
